question: Does a searched early EndTurn improve exact terminal outcomes after the root keeps using the same three-turn teacher instead of reverting to the direct model?
method: From the existing fit dataset, take the first identical-prefix early-stop position on each of the first16 eligible independent maps in ascending seed and record order. Force the teacher-selected or static complete root turn from the same replayed state, verify exact exported post-turn observations, then continue both branches with the persistent native three-turn root and frozen routed-v6 direct opponent. Censor action-limit games rather than scoring adjudications. No student model is involved.
interpretation: Under persistent root search, forcing the early stop helped more often than continuing this static plan in the small fixed subset, but the independent-map sign test is inconclusive. This is not a validated policy advantage.
Even large positive conditional three-turn score gaps can disagree with eventual terminal outcomes in either direction. Search score is not an exact terminal credit label.
This selected fit-only subset is neither an unbiased estimate over future maps nor evidence that the failed neural student improved. No training, rating, browser agent or game rule changed.
verification: Predeclared protocol commit c87cadf preceded branch outcomes. Remote nice19 pinned one-core run completed within its20-minute cap; 421 Python tests and Ruff check/format passed. All16 forced candidate branches reproduced the exported native post-turn observation exactly.
qualification: Exploratory post hoc subset of already-used fit maps, with one selected position per map and 16 independent maps total. It is not fresh held-out validation, Elo, proof of causality for persistent search strength, or a student promotion gate.
